name: web
description: Fetch a public web page as readable markdown, and search if an API key is set. Guarded against SSRF, with a size cap and per-host rate limit.
author: Adaptive Agent Harness

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a public http(s) URL and return the page as markdown: headings, lists, links and code preserved, scripts and styling removed. Use this to read a documentation page, an article, a spec or a changelog. Refuses private, loopback and link-local addresses (including a public hostname that resolves to one), refuses any scheme other than http/https, caps the body at 5 MB, follows at most 5 redirects, and allows 5 requests per host per minute. If you only need to know whether a page is worth reading, call read_result first.

url.description: The full http:// or https:// URL to fetch. A bare hostname is not enough, and a non-http(s) scheme is refused. Must be a public address: private, loopback and link-local targets are refused even if the name looks public.

max_chars.description: How many characters of markdown to return. The default of 20000 is roughly a full article. Raise it for long documentation, lower it to save context. The page itself is capped at 5 MB regardless.

tools.name: read_result
tools.description: Fetch a URL and report its shape -- final URL after redirects, HTTP status, content type, byte size, how much readable text it holds -- plus the first few thousand characters. Cheaper than web_fetch for deciding whether the rest of a page is worth reading, which is what it is for. Same SSRF guard, size cap and rate limit as web_fetch.

url.description: The full http:// or https:// URL to inspect. Non-http(s) schemes and private or loopback targets are refused.

max_chars.description: How many characters of the page to preview. The size and type summary is returned in full regardless.

tools.name: web_query
tools.description: Search the web and return titles, URLs and snippets. Requires BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY (or ADAPTIVE_HARNESS_SEARCH_API_KEY) in the environment; with no key it returns a message saying so and does nothing else, so it is safe to call before you know. Named web_query rather than web_search because the harness already ships a built-in web_search tool and a plugin cannot shadow a built-in. Prefer web_fetch when you already have a URL.

query.description: The search terms. Plain keywords work best; natural-language questions return worse results.

limit.description: How many results to return. Defaults to 5.
